analysis.assessment: As of 2025-03-12T12:15:00Z the available evidence shows a third, strongest upstream microbiological action-level excursion on Famotidine Injection, LINE-A: in-progress BATCH-099 has an upstream bioburden result at 171% of its action limit (LAB-0300, 1.71 action-limit ratio) and a concurrent action-level environmental signal at 109% of the EM action limit (EM-0100, 1.09) bearing gram-negative morphology in the process support area. The two prior events (BATCH-075 at 123%, BATCH-084 at 148%) each led to high-severity microbiology deviations that are still open with empty root-cause cells, and both batches were released and shipped; affected product may already be in distribution. No deviation record exists yet for BATCH-099, and no release-justification, routing-policy, recipe/controller/calibration, raw-replicate or EM-sampling-plan evidence is in the scoped package. Equipment signals are ambiguous: BATCH-099's PUMP-02 pressure ratio is in-range at 95.9% of its limit, but two historical PUMP-02 exceedances (1.24 vs 1.1) occurred on SYN-0015 and SYN-0090 (the open DEV-0007 batch), one day after a PUMP-02 inspection. All twelve screening priority candidates proved to be clock-binding record artifacts, not process faults. Proposed routing (advisory; no approved policy in package): L1 cross-functional project for the microbiological recurrence with retrospective review of shipped batches; L2 for the PUMP-02/DEV-0007 equipment question and the DEV-0008 recurrence determination pending linkage; L3 for closed low-severity procedure deviations and records remediation. This investigation does not approve or execute any disposition, release, CAPA or notification - all such decisions are routed to human review with the coordination tasks listed. Advisory routing proposal in the absence of an in-scope approved policy: L1 (highest-priority cross-functional project): the recurring upstream microbiological excursion series on Famotidine Injection/LINE-A - current BATCH-099 event, environmental assessment of the process support area, retrospective impact review of released/shipped BATCH-075 and BATCH-084, and organism identification. L2 (standard cross-functional investigation): PUMP-02 equipment deviation DEV-0007 including both 1.24 exceedances (merge to L1 if linked to the microbiology series), and DEV-0008 recurrence determination. L3 (local/departmental handling): closed low-severity procedure deviations DEV-0001/0002/0004/0006, PUMP-02 ratio monitoring, and records remediation (missing SYN-0097 disposition, process-clock binding, image-only PDF review). Final severity and routing must be set by the site's approved versioned routing policy, which is not in the evidence package.

draft_report.assessment: As of 2025-03-12T12:15:00Z the available evidence shows a third, strongest upstream microbiological action-level excursion on Famotidine Injection, LINE-A: in-progress BATCH-099 has an upstream bioburden result at 171% of its action limit (LAB-0300, 1.71 action-limit ratio) and a concurrent action-level environmental signal at 109% of the EM action limit (EM-0100, 1.09) bearing gram-negative morphology in the process support area. The two prior events (BATCH-075 at 123%, BATCH-084 at 148%) each led to high-severity microbiology deviations that are still open with empty root-cause cells, and both batches were released and shipped; affected product may already be in distribution. No deviation record exists yet for BATCH-099, and no release-justification, routing-policy, recipe/controller/calibration, raw-replicate or EM-sampling-plan evidence is in the scoped package. Equipment signals are ambiguous: BATCH-099's PUMP-02 pressure ratio is in-range at 95.9% of its limit, but two historical PUMP-02 exceedances (1.24 vs 1.1) occurred on SYN-0015 and SYN-0090 (the open DEV-0007 batch), one day after a PUMP-02 inspection. All twelve screening priority candidates proved to be clock-binding record artifacts, not process faults. Proposed routing (advisory; no approved policy in package): L1 cross-functional project for the microbiological recurrence with retrospective review of shipped batches; L2 for the PUMP-02/DEV-0007 equipment question and the DEV-0008 recurrence determination pending linkage; L3 for closed low-severity procedure deviations and records remediation. This investigation does not approve or execute any disposition, release, CAPA or notification - all such decisions are routed to human review with the coordination tasks listed. Advisory routing proposal in the absence of an in-scope approved policy: L1 (highest-priority cross-functional project): the recurring upstream microbiological excursion series on Famotidine Injection/LINE-A - current BATCH-099 event, environmental assessment of the process support area, retrospective impact review of released/shipped BATCH-075 and BATCH-084, and organism identification. L2 (standard cross-functional investigation): PUMP-02 equipment deviation DEV-0007 including both 1.24 exceedances (merge to L1 if linked to the microbiology series), and DEV-0008 recurrence determination. L3 (local/departmental handling): closed low-severity procedure deviations DEV-0001/0002/0004/0006, PUMP-02 ratio monitoring, and records remediation (missing SYN-0097 disposition, process-clock binding, image-only PDF review). Final severity and routing must be set by the site's approved versioned routing policy, which is not in the evidence package.

draft_report.cross_scope_synthesis: Shared pattern: three independent specialist reviews plus the lead deep-dive converge on a recurring upstream microbiological excursion series on Famotidine Injection, LINE-A - BATCH-075 (123% of action limit, 2024-12-01), BATCH-084 (148%, 2025-01-04), BATCH-099 (171%, 2025-03-12, in progress) - now accompanied for the first time by an action-level environmental signal (109% of the EM action limit) with gram-negative morphology in the process support area, ten minutes after the upstream sample. Review of the deterministic screening extrema extends the context: an earlier action-level event on SYN-0004 (1.08, Electrolyte, LINE-C, 2024-02-21) has no deviation record (the scoped deviation log starts 2024-03-28), an invalidated 1.06 repeat with a normal resample occurred on SYN-0014 (2024-04-01, invalidation reason not recorded), and seven alert-level upstream results span LINE-A/B/C products between Feb and Dec 2024 (SYN-0001, SYN-0015, SYN-0018, SYN-0029, SYN-0032, SYN-0036, SYN-0082). Exceptions and quiet signals: everything else reviewed is clean - 98/98 populated batch dispositions read 'released', 100/100 operator events are routine, work orders are 12/12 planned inspections with no corrective work, finished-product endotoxin passed for the two shipped affected batches, EM has exactly six at/above-alert rows (all dispositioned), and the historian has exactly 2 of 400 events out of range - both PUMP-02 equipment_pressure_ratio 1.24 vs 1.1 on SYN-0015 (2024-04-05) and SYN-0090 (2025-01-30, one day after PUMP-02 work order WO-0010, and the batch of open equipment deviation DEV-0007). Cross-cutting control gaps: both earlier affected batches were released and shipped while their high-severity microbiology deviations remain open with empty root-cause cells and no release-justification records; DEV-0008 (procedure, high, open) is the only recurrence-flagged deviation and its linkage to the series is undetermined; the lab has precedent for invalidating a high result (SYN-0014) but the three cluster events carry 'action' status with no recorded invalidation or resample. Record-quality limits: all 12 screening priority candidates are clock-binding artifacts with in-limits values (no process clocks on lab/historian series; bridge alignment rejected; historian event IDs shuffled vs file rows; image-only scanned PDF needs human visual review and its OCR covers only early records; single reported ratio values without raw replicates; lab modalities are duplicate exports of one canonical dataset, so agreement is not independent confirmation). Missing evidence that could change actions: organism speciation, release justifications, the EM sampling plan, raw assay replicates, recipe/controller/calibration records, and the approved L1/L2/L3 routing policy (none in the scoped package).

interpretations.statement: LAB-0225, LAB-0255 and LAB-0300 are genuine action-limit exceedances of the upstream bioburden signal: each result exceeds its action limit per the linked percentage metrics and its 'action' status is consistent across all three lab modalities.

BATCH-075 and BATCH-084 show an alert-then-action pattern within one day (PRE-LAB-001 0.79 alert at 11:15Z then LAB-0225 1.23 action at 12:00Z; PRE-LAB-002 0.82 alert at 11:40Z then LAB-0255 1.48 action at 12:25Z). BATCH-099 shows a single action-level result with no preceding alert-level pre-lab record. The confirmatory LAB samples were collected minutes before the PRE-LAB samples, so 'PRE-LAB' denotes a faster result path, not an earlier process sample.

Environmental monitoring shows same-day excursions for all three batches in the same 'process support area' location: alert-level for BATCH-075/084 and action-level for BATCH-099 with organism 'gram-negative morphology'. Record chronology places the EM-0100 record between LAB-0300 sample collection and result availability. This is record-time association only; no causal direction is established, and EM and bioburden are different sample types.

All ten clock-quality candidates are record/time-basis artifacts rather than process faults: their values are inside limits with normal statuses, except that the lims_review_local candidate's second member row is the real BATCH-099 action record - the flag itself concerns time, not the value. The lab sources carry explicit UTC record timestamps but no resolved process-clock basis, and lims_review_local carries no sample times at all (release timestamps only).

missing_source_time flags apply to every numeric screening entry in lims_export, microbiology and environmental_monitoring, plus the single lims_review_local series; the ten candidates are coverage samples of this source-wide clock-basis condition, not entity-specific signals. No candidate flag indicates a process fault by itself.

No PRE-LAB alert record exists for BATCH-099 in any scoped lab source. Either no pre-lab (early-warning) sample was taken/recorded for BATCH-099, or such a record is missing from the export. Context from deterministic screening: SYN-0014 also has an action-level result without a PRE-LAB row (row not re-read in this run), so BATCH-099 is not unique in this export; but unlike BATCH-075/084 it reached action level with no in-export early-warning record.

All four open deviations (DEV-0003, DEV-0005, DEV-0007, DEV-0008) attach to batches that were released and shipped before the cutoff, so open investigations - including three high-severity ones and the only recurrence-flagged deviation - coexist with product already in distribution.

Each of the four open deviations was opened during the linked batch's manufacturing window (opened_at falls between the batch start_time and end_time), so the deviations are in-process events, not post-release discoveries in the record.

The scoped quality-record sources contain no non-routine operational signal: no quarantined or rejected batch (98/98 status and disposition cells read 'released') and no non-routine operator event (100/100 'batch_check'/'normal'). The deviation register is the only quality-signal carrier in this scope.

BATCH-099 behaves like a normally in-progress batch: it started 2025-03-12T06:55:00Z, received a routine operator batch_check at 08:10:00Z, has no deviation in the register, and its missing status/disposition cells are consistent with an unfinished batch rather than a recorded failure.

SYN-0097 is a records gap distinct from BATCH-099: its manufacture ended 2025-02-27T15:11:29Z, yet no disposition or ship record exists as of the 2025-03-12T12:15:00Z as_of - roughly thirteen days with no recorded disposition decision.

source_review.pdf is a redundant summary of deviations.csv: it reproduces all deviations (count certified by M-dev-record-count) on deviation_id/batch/opened_at with no additional fields, and adds only a synthetic-data banner.

The package is explicitly synthetic: the manifest notice states all factory records are reconstructed synthetic data, and every read row in deviations, batch_records and operator_events carries provenance 'synthetic_factory_signal'. Findings inform the exercise, not real product state.

The exact cross-modality agreement reflects duplicate exports of one canonical dataset rather than independent confirmations: microbiology_results.xlsx duplicates lims_export row-for-row, lims_review_local restates the same results as percent-of-limit with converted local times, and all rows carry provenance 'synthetic_factory_signal'.

BATCH-099 has a confirmed action-level upstream bioburden excursion (171% of its stated action limit) in an in-progress sterile injectable batch, with a concurrent action-level environmental signal (109% of the EM action limit) bearing gram-negative morphology in the process support area. Under ordinary pharmaceutical control logic this warrants immediate batch hold assessment and deviation opening; that decision belongs to QA, not to this investigation.

The three action-level upstream bioburden events on Famotidine Injection, LINE-A (BATCH-075 123%, BATCH-084 148%, BATCH-099 171% of the action limit) form an escalating cluster across roughly three and a half months, and both earlier batches were released and shipped while their high-severity microbiology deviations remain open. Deterministic screening extrema place this cluster inside a longer, multi-line history of upstream bioburden alert/action signals: an earlier action-level event on SYN-0004 (1.08, Electrolyte Injection, LINE-C, 2024-02) with no deviation record, an invalidated 1.06 repeat with a normal resample on SYN-0014 (2024-04), and seven alert-level results across LINE-A/B/C products between 2024-02 and 2024-12. Common cause is not established by these records alone; the recent cluster is distinguished by same product/line, escalation, open high-severity deviations and shipment of affected batches.

The two prior events each had a preceding alert-level upstream result (PRE-LAB-001 0.79, PRE-LAB-002 0.82) and an alert-level EM result, while the current event reached action level in both the process sample and the environment with an identified gram-negative morphology. This progression is consistent with a persistent or recurring contamination source in the shared manufacturing environment, but the evidence does not identify a source, and no organism observation exists for the two earlier EM rows.

All twelve screening priority candidates are clock-quality flags (missing_source_time) on limit/result cells whose underlying values sit inside their stated limits; they indicate missing elapsed-hours process clocks and limited alignment capability in these lab/historian series, not process faults. Cross-series alignment for the BATCH-099 signals cannot be certified on process clocks; only record-timestamp ordering is available.

No L1/L2/L3 routing policy, severity matrix or release-justification record exists in the scoped package, so any severity or routing proposal from this investigation is advisory and must be reconciled against the site's approved versioned routing policy before use.

BATCH-099's four historian events are all severity 'normal' and inside their expected bands; its PUMP-02 equipment_pressure_ratio (1.0552) sits 0.0448 below the 1.1 limit (11th highest of 100 band events). However, a whole-file scan found exactly 2 of 400 historian events out of range - both PUMP-02 equipment_pressure_ratio 1.24 vs limit 1.1, on SYN-0015 (2024-04-05) and SYN-0090 (2025-01-30, one day after PUMP-02 work order WO-0010). SYN-0090 is the batch of the still-open equipment deviation DEV-0007. Equipment contribution to the microbiological events is unproven but has concrete supporting signals.

BATCH-099 shows no process fault in the scoped historian evidence: all four events are inside their expected bands and labeled severity normal, including the PUMP-02 equipment_pressure_ratio event (1.0552, an upper-tail in-band value 0.0448 below its expected high limit per metric m-b99-margin). A single upper-tail value within band is not evidence of an equipment fault; the two out-of-range events belong to other batches (metrics m-oor-count, m-pr-max).
interpretations.uncertainty: Distribution context is descriptive only; no statistical significance or process capability claim is made.

interpretations.statement: The equipment_pressure_ratio expected band on PUMP-02 is established by direct reads of the BATCH-099, SYN-0017 and SYN-0064 anchor rows and by the full band census (metrics m-band-n, m-hist-count): four distinct bands with an equal number of events per band and four events per batch leave no room for a second parameter inside the equipment_pressure_ratio band if every batch carries the same parameters. The two out-of-range events therefore fall in the PUMP-02 band (metric m-oor-count).
interpretations.uncertainty: Parameter text cells were read for 3 anchor rows plus BATCH-099/SYN-0017/SYN-0064 full rows only; the attribution for the other 97 batches is structural inference, and rows 60/368 parameter cells were not individually read.

interpretations.statement: The missing_source_time / clock_quality flags on the two screening candidates are acquisition/record artifacts, not process faults: every flagged row carries complete, identical timestamp and occurred_at ISO-8601 UTC text cells, all values are inside their expected bands, and severity is normal. The file-wide flag condition covers every historian series (see metric m-hist-count) while the parsed occurred_at column is populated for every event, so the flag reflects clock binding, not missing source timestamps.
interpretations.uncertainty: Interpretation requires human review; the bridge clock binding may be restorable from the timestamp cells, which would remove the flag without changing any source value.

interpretations.statement: The historian cannot support process-clock-aligned temporal analysis as ingested: time_basis is unresolved file-wide, so any temporal comparison must cite the raw timestamp/occurred_at text cells (record timestamps) rather than time_value. The two work-order files and the PDF likewise provide record timestamps only.
interpretations.uncertainty: Cross-source clock alignment (e.g., work-order clock vs historian clock) is not established; the timestamps carry explicit Z (UTC) designations but no independent synchronization evidence.

interpretations.statement: process_event_points.pdf mirrors historian_export.csv for every sampled point and explicitly disclaims interpolated trajectories; it adds no information beyond the historian rows and cannot be used to infer continuous process behavior.

interpretations.statement: The two work-order files are duplicate representations of the same twelve records (planned inspections only) and therefore do not provide independent corroboration of maintenance history; in particular there is no record of any corrective action, repair, or calibration follow-up for PUMP-02 after its exceedance in the equipment_pressure_ratio band (metrics m-oor-count, m-pr-max).

analysis.cross_scope_synthesis: Shared pattern: three independent specialist reviews plus the lead deep-dive converge on a recurring upstream microbiological excursion series on Famotidine Injection, LINE-A - BATCH-075 (123% of action limit, 2024-12-01), BATCH-084 (148%, 2025-01-04), BATCH-099 (171%, 2025-03-12, in progress) - now accompanied for the first time by an action-level environmental signal (109% of the EM action limit) with gram-negative morphology in the process support area, ten minutes after the upstream sample. Review of the deterministic screening extrema extends the context: an earlier action-level event on SYN-0004 (1.08, Electrolyte, LINE-C, 2024-02-21) has no deviation record (the scoped deviation log starts 2024-03-28), an invalidated 1.06 repeat with a normal resample occurred on SYN-0014 (2024-04-01, invalidation reason not recorded), and seven alert-level upstream results span LINE-A/B/C products between Feb and Dec 2024 (SYN-0001, SYN-0015, SYN-0018, SYN-0029, SYN-0032, SYN-0036, SYN-0082). Exceptions and quiet signals: everything else reviewed is clean - 98/98 populated batch dispositions read 'released', 100/100 operator events are routine, work orders are 12/12 planned inspections with no corrective work, finished-product endotoxin passed for the two shipped affected batches, EM has exactly six at/above-alert rows (all dispositioned), and the historian has exactly 2 of 400 events out of range - both PUMP-02 equipment_pressure_ratio 1.24 vs 1.1 on SYN-0015 (2024-04-05) and SYN-0090 (2025-01-30, one day after PUMP-02 work order WO-0010, and the batch of open equipment deviation DEV-0007). Cross-cutting control gaps: both earlier affected batches were released and shipped while their high-severity microbiology deviations remain open with empty root-cause cells and no release-justification records; DEV-0008 (procedure, high, open) is the only recurrence-flagged deviation and its linkage to the series is undetermined; the lab has precedent for invalidating a high result (SYN-0014) but the three cluster events carry 'action' status with no recorded invalidation or resample. Record-quality limits: all 12 screening priority candidates are clock-binding artifacts with in-limits values (no process clocks on lab/historian series; bridge alignment rejected; historian event IDs shuffled vs file rows; image-only scanned PDF needs human visual review and its OCR covers only early records; single reported ratio values without raw replicates; lab modalities are duplicate exports of one canonical dataset, so agreement is not independent confirmation). Missing evidence that could change actions: organism speciation, release justifications, the EM sampling plan, raw assay replicates, recipe/controller/calibration records, and the approved L1/L2/L3 routing policy (none in the scoped package).

interpretations.statement: LAB-0225, LAB-0255 and LAB-0300 are genuine action-limit exceedances of the upstream bioburden signal: each result exceeds its action limit per the linked percentage metrics and its 'action' status is consistent across all three lab modalities.

BATCH-075 and BATCH-084 show an alert-then-action pattern within one day (PRE-LAB-001 0.79 alert at 11:15Z then LAB-0225 1.23 action at 12:00Z; PRE-LAB-002 0.82 alert at 11:40Z then LAB-0255 1.48 action at 12:25Z). BATCH-099 shows a single action-level result with no preceding alert-level pre-lab record. The confirmatory LAB samples were collected minutes before the PRE-LAB samples, so 'PRE-LAB' denotes a faster result path, not an earlier process sample.

Environmental monitoring shows same-day excursions for all three batches in the same 'process support area' location: alert-level for BATCH-075/084 and action-level for BATCH-099 with organism 'gram-negative morphology'. Record chronology places the EM-0100 record between LAB-0300 sample collection and result availability. This is record-time association only; no causal direction is established, and EM and bioburden are different sample types.

All ten clock-quality candidates are record/time-basis artifacts rather than process faults: their values are inside limits with normal statuses, except that the lims_review_local candidate's second member row is the real BATCH-099 action record - the flag itself concerns time, not the value. The lab sources carry explicit UTC record timestamps but no resolved process-clock basis, and lims_review_local carries no sample times at all (release timestamps only).

missing_source_time flags apply to every numeric screening entry in lims_export, microbiology and environmental_monitoring, plus the single lims_review_local series; the ten candidates are coverage samples of this source-wide clock-basis condition, not entity-specific signals. No candidate flag indicates a process fault by itself.

No PRE-LAB alert record exists for BATCH-099 in any scoped lab source. Either no pre-lab (early-warning) sample was taken/recorded for BATCH-099, or such a record is missing from the export. Context from deterministic screening: SYN-0014 also has an action-level result without a PRE-LAB row (row not re-read in this run), so BATCH-099 is not unique in this export; but unlike BATCH-075/084 it reached action level with no in-export early-warning record.

All four open deviations (DEV-0003, DEV-0005, DEV-0007, DEV-0008) attach to batches that were released and shipped before the cutoff, so open investigations - including three high-severity ones and the only recurrence-flagged deviation - coexist with product already in distribution.

Each of the four open deviations was opened during the linked batch's manufacturing window (opened_at falls between the batch start_time and end_time), so the deviations are in-process events, not post-release discoveries in the record.

The scoped quality-record sources contain no non-routine operational signal: no quarantined or rejected batch (98/98 status and disposition cells read 'released') and no non-routine operator event (100/100 'batch_check'/'normal'). The deviation register is the only quality-signal carrier in this scope.

BATCH-099 behaves like a normally in-progress batch: it started 2025-03-12T06:55:00Z, received a routine operator batch_check at 08:10:00Z, has no deviation in the register, and its missing status/disposition cells are consistent with an unfinished batch rather than a recorded failure.

SYN-0097 is a records gap distinct from BATCH-099: its manufacture ended 2025-02-27T15:11:29Z, yet no disposition or ship record exists as of the 2025-03-12T12:15:00Z as_of - roughly thirteen days with no recorded disposition decision.

source_review.pdf is a redundant summary of deviations.csv: it reproduces all deviations (count certified by M-dev-record-count) on deviation_id/batch/opened_at with no additional fields, and adds only a synthetic-data banner.

The package is explicitly synthetic: the manifest notice states all factory records are reconstructed synthetic data, and every read row in deviations, batch_records and operator_events carries provenance 'synthetic_factory_signal'. Findings inform the exercise, not real product state.

The exact cross-modality agreement reflects duplicate exports of one canonical dataset rather than independent confirmations: microbiology_results.xlsx duplicates lims_export row-for-row, lims_review_local restates the same results as percent-of-limit with converted local times, and all rows carry provenance 'synthetic_factory_signal'.

BATCH-099 has a confirmed action-level upstream bioburden excursion (171% of its stated action limit) in an in-progress sterile injectable batch, with a concurrent action-level environmental signal (109% of the EM action limit) bearing gram-negative morphology in the process support area. Under ordinary pharmaceutical control logic this warrants immediate batch hold assessment and deviation opening; that decision belongs to QA, not to this investigation.

The three action-level upstream bioburden events on Famotidine Injection, LINE-A (BATCH-075 123%, BATCH-084 148%, BATCH-099 171% of the action limit) form an escalating cluster across roughly three and a half months, and both earlier batches were released and shipped while their high-severity microbiology deviations remain open. Deterministic screening extrema place this cluster inside a longer, multi-line history of upstream bioburden alert/action signals: an earlier action-level event on SYN-0004 (1.08, Electrolyte Injection, LINE-C, 2024-02) with no deviation record, an invalidated 1.06 repeat with a normal resample on SYN-0014 (2024-04), and seven alert-level results across LINE-A/B/C products between 2024-02 and 2024-12. Common cause is not established by these records alone; the recent cluster is distinguished by same product/line, escalation, open high-severity deviations and shipment of affected batches.

The two prior events each had a preceding alert-level upstream result (PRE-LAB-001 0.79, PRE-LAB-002 0.82) and an alert-level EM result, while the current event reached action level in both the process sample and the environment with an identified gram-negative morphology. This progression is consistent with a persistent or recurring contamination source in the shared manufacturing environment, but the evidence does not identify a source, and no organism observation exists for the two earlier EM rows.

All twelve screening priority candidates are clock-quality flags (missing_source_time) on limit/result cells whose underlying values sit inside their stated limits; they indicate missing elapsed-hours process clocks and limited alignment capability in these lab/historian series, not process faults. Cross-series alignment for the BATCH-099 signals cannot be certified on process clocks; only record-timestamp ordering is available.

No L1/L2/L3 routing policy, severity matrix or release-justification record exists in the scoped package, so any severity or routing proposal from this investigation is advisory and must be reconciled against the site's approved versioned routing policy before use.

BATCH-099's four historian events are all severity 'normal' and inside their expected bands; its PUMP-02 equipment_pressure_ratio (1.0552) sits 0.0448 below the 1.1 limit (11th highest of 100 band events). However, a whole-file scan found exactly 2 of 400 historian events out of range - both PUMP-02 equipment_pressure_ratio 1.24 vs limit 1.1, on SYN-0015 (2024-04-05) and SYN-0090 (2025-01-30, one day after PUMP-02 work order WO-0010). SYN-0090 is the batch of the still-open equipment deviation DEV-0007. Equipment contribution to the microbiological events is unproven but has concrete supporting signals.

BATCH-099 shows no process fault in the scoped historian evidence: all four events are inside their expected bands and labeled severity normal, including the PUMP-02 equipment_pressure_ratio event (1.0552, an upper-tail in-band value 0.0448 below its expected high limit per metric m-b99-margin). A single upper-tail value within band is not evidence of an equipment fault; the two out-of-range events belong to other batches (metrics m-oor-count, m-pr-max).
interpretations.uncertainty: Distribution context is descriptive only; no statistical significance or process capability claim is made.

interpretations.statement: The equipment_pressure_ratio expected band on PUMP-02 is established by direct reads of the BATCH-099, SYN-0017 and SYN-0064 anchor rows and by the full band census (metrics m-band-n, m-hist-count): four distinct bands with an equal number of events per band and four events per batch leave no room for a second parameter inside the equipment_pressure_ratio band if every batch carries the same parameters. The two out-of-range events therefore fall in the PUMP-02 band (metric m-oor-count).
interpretations.uncertainty: Parameter text cells were read for 3 anchor rows plus BATCH-099/SYN-0017/SYN-0064 full rows only; the attribution for the other 97 batches is structural inference, and rows 60/368 parameter cells were not individually read.

interpretations.statement: The missing_source_time / clock_quality flags on the two screening candidates are acquisition/record artifacts, not process faults: every flagged row carries complete, identical timestamp and occurred_at ISO-8601 UTC text cells, all values are inside their expected bands, and severity is normal. The file-wide flag condition covers every historian series (see metric m-hist-count) while the parsed occurred_at column is populated for every event, so the flag reflects clock binding, not missing source timestamps.
interpretations.uncertainty: Interpretation requires human review; the bridge clock binding may be restorable from the timestamp cells, which would remove the flag without changing any source value.

workflow.assessment: As of 2025-03-12T12:15:00Z the available evidence shows a third, strongest upstream microbiological action-level excursion on Famotidine Injection, LINE-A: in-progress BATCH-099 has an upstream bioburden result at 171% of its action limit (LAB-0300, 1.71 action-limit ratio) and a concurrent action-level environmental signal at 109% of the EM action limit (EM-0100, 1.09) bearing gram-negative morphology in the process support area. The two prior events (BATCH-075 at 123%, BATCH-084 at 148%) each led to high-severity microbiology deviations that are still open with empty root-cause cells, and both batches were released and shipped; affected product may already be in distribution. No deviation record exists yet for BATCH-099, and no release-justification, routing-policy, recipe/controller/calibration, raw-replicate or EM-sampling-plan evidence is in the scoped package. Equipment signals are ambiguous: BATCH-099's PUMP-02 pressure ratio is in-range at 95.9% of its limit, but two historical PUMP-02 exceedances (1.24 vs 1.1) occurred on SYN-0015 and SYN-0090 (the open DEV-0007 batch), one day after a PUMP-02 inspection. All twelve screening priority candidates proved to be clock-binding record artifacts, not process faults. Proposed routing (advisory; no approved policy in package): L1 cross-functional project for the microbiological recurrence with retrospective review of shipped batches; L2 for the PUMP-02/DEV-0007 equipment question and the DEV-0008 recurrence determination pending linkage; L3 for closed low-severity procedure deviations and records remediation. This investigation does not approve or execute any disposition, release, CAPA or notification - all such decisions are routed to human review with the coordination tasks listed. Advisory routing proposal in the absence of an in-scope approved policy: L1 (highest-priority cross-functional project): the recurring upstream microbiological excursion series on Famotidine Injection/LINE-A - current BATCH-099 event, environmental assessment of the process support area, retrospective impact review of released/shipped BATCH-075 and BATCH-084, and organism identification. L2 (standard cross-functional investigation): PUMP-02 equipment deviation DEV-0007 including both 1.24 exceedances (merge to L1 if linked to the microbiology series), and DEV-0008 recurrence determination. L3 (local/departmental handling): closed low-severity procedure deviations DEV-0001/0002/0004/0006, PUMP-02 ratio monitoring, and records remediation (missing SYN-0097 disposition, process-clock binding, image-only PDF review). Final severity and routing must be set by the site's approved versioned routing policy, which is not in the evidence package.

workflow.cross_scope_synthesis: Shared pattern: three independent specialist reviews plus the lead deep-dive converge on a recurring upstream microbiological excursion series on Famotidine Injection, LINE-A - BATCH-075 (123% of action limit, 2024-12-01), BATCH-084 (148%, 2025-01-04), BATCH-099 (171%, 2025-03-12, in progress) - now accompanied for the first time by an action-level environmental signal (109% of the EM action limit) with gram-negative morphology in the process support area, ten minutes after the upstream sample. Review of the deterministic screening extrema extends the context: an earlier action-level event on SYN-0004 (1.08, Electrolyte, LINE-C, 2024-02-21) has no deviation record (the scoped deviation log starts 2024-03-28), an invalidated 1.06 repeat with a normal resample occurred on SYN-0014 (2024-04-01, invalidation reason not recorded), and seven alert-level upstream results span LINE-A/B/C products between Feb and Dec 2024 (SYN-0001, SYN-0015, SYN-0018, SYN-0029, SYN-0032, SYN-0036, SYN-0082). Exceptions and quiet signals: everything else reviewed is clean - 98/98 populated batch dispositions read 'released', 100/100 operator events are routine, work orders are 12/12 planned inspections with no corrective work, finished-product endotoxin passed for the two shipped affected batches, EM has exactly six at/above-alert rows (all dispositioned), and the historian has exactly 2 of 400 events out of range - both PUMP-02 equipment_pressure_ratio 1.24 vs 1.1 on SYN-0015 (2024-04-05) and SYN-0090 (2025-01-30, one day after PUMP-02 work order WO-0010, and the batch of open equipment deviation DEV-0007). Cross-cutting control gaps: both earlier affected batches were released and shipped while their high-severity microbiology deviations remain open with empty root-cause cells and no release-justification records; DEV-0008 (procedure, high, open) is the only recurrence-flagged deviation and its linkage to the series is undetermined; the lab has precedent for invalidating a high result (SYN-0014) but the three cluster events carry 'action' status with no recorded invalidation or resample. Record-quality limits: all 12 screening priority candidates are clock-binding artifacts with in-limits values (no process clocks on lab/historian series; bridge alignment rejected; historian event IDs shuffled vs file rows; image-only scanned PDF needs human visual review and its OCR covers only early records; single reported ratio values without raw replicates; lab modalities are duplicate exports of one canonical dataset, so agreement is not independent confirmation). Missing evidence that could change actions: organism speciation, release justifications, the EM sampling plan, raw assay replicates, recipe/controller/calibration records, and the approved L1/L2/L3 routing policy (none in the scoped package).

interpretations.statement: LAB-0225, LAB-0255 and LAB-0300 are genuine action-limit exceedances of the upstream bioburden signal: each result exceeds its action limit per the linked percentage metrics and its 'action' status is consistent across all three lab modalities.

BATCH-075 and BATCH-084 show an alert-then-action pattern within one day (PRE-LAB-001 0.79 alert at 11:15Z then LAB-0225 1.23 action at 12:00Z; PRE-LAB-002 0.82 alert at 11:40Z then LAB-0255 1.48 action at 12:25Z). BATCH-099 shows a single action-level result with no preceding alert-level pre-lab record. The confirmatory LAB samples were collected minutes before the PRE-LAB samples, so 'PRE-LAB' denotes a faster result path, not an earlier process sample.

Environmental monitoring shows same-day excursions for all three batches in the same 'process support area' location: alert-level for BATCH-075/084 and action-level for BATCH-099 with organism 'gram-negative morphology'. Record chronology places the EM-0100 record between LAB-0300 sample collection and result availability. This is record-time association only; no causal direction is established, and EM and bioburden are different sample types.

All ten clock-quality candidates are record/time-basis artifacts rather than process faults: their values are inside limits with normal statuses, except that the lims_review_local candidate's second member row is the real BATCH-099 action record - the flag itself concerns time, not the value. The lab sources carry explicit UTC record timestamps but no resolved process-clock basis, and lims_review_local carries no sample times at all (release timestamps only).

missing_source_time flags apply to every numeric screening entry in lims_export, microbiology and environmental_monitoring, plus the single lims_review_local series; the ten candidates are coverage samples of this source-wide clock-basis condition, not entity-specific signals. No candidate flag indicates a process fault by itself.

No PRE-LAB alert record exists for BATCH-099 in any scoped lab source. Either no pre-lab (early-warning) sample was taken/recorded for BATCH-099, or such a record is missing from the export. Context from deterministic screening: SYN-0014 also has an action-level result without a PRE-LAB row (row not re-read in this run), so BATCH-099 is not unique in this export; but unlike BATCH-075/084 it reached action level with no in-export early-warning record.

All four open deviations (DEV-0003, DEV-0005, DEV-0007, DEV-0008) attach to batches that were released and shipped before the cutoff, so open investigations - including three high-severity ones and the only recurrence-flagged deviation - coexist with product already in distribution.

Each of the four open deviations was opened during the linked batch's manufacturing window (opened_at falls between the batch start_time and end_time), so the deviations are in-process events, not post-release discoveries in the record.

The scoped quality-record sources contain no non-routine operational signal: no quarantined or rejected batch (98/98 status and disposition cells read 'released') and no non-routine operator event (100/100 'batch_check'/'normal'). The deviation register is the only quality-signal carrier in this scope.

BATCH-099 behaves like a normally in-progress batch: it started 2025-03-12T06:55:00Z, received a routine operator batch_check at 08:10:00Z, has no deviation in the register, and its missing status/disposition cells are consistent with an unfinished batch rather than a recorded failure.

SYN-0097 is a records gap distinct from BATCH-099: its manufacture ended 2025-02-27T15:11:29Z, yet no disposition or ship record exists as of the 2025-03-12T12:15:00Z as_of - roughly thirteen days with no recorded disposition decision.

source_review.pdf is a redundant summary of deviations.csv: it reproduces all deviations (count certified by M-dev-record-count) on deviation_id/batch/opened_at with no additional fields, and adds only a synthetic-data banner.

The package is explicitly synthetic: the manifest notice states all factory records are reconstructed synthetic data, and every read row in deviations, batch_records and operator_events carries provenance 'synthetic_factory_signal'. Findings inform the exercise, not real product state.

The exact cross-modality agreement reflects duplicate exports of one canonical dataset rather than independent confirmations: microbiology_results.xlsx duplicates lims_export row-for-row, lims_review_local restates the same results as percent-of-limit with converted local times, and all rows carry provenance 'synthetic_factory_signal'.

BATCH-099 has a confirmed action-level upstream bioburden excursion (171% of its stated action limit) in an in-progress sterile injectable batch, with a concurrent action-level environmental signal (109% of the EM action limit) bearing gram-negative morphology in the process support area. Under ordinary pharmaceutical control logic this warrants immediate batch hold assessment and deviation opening; that decision belongs to QA, not to this investigation.

The three action-level upstream bioburden events on Famotidine Injection, LINE-A (BATCH-075 123%, BATCH-084 148%, BATCH-099 171% of the action limit) form an escalating cluster across roughly three and a half months, and both earlier batches were released and shipped while their high-severity microbiology deviations remain open. Deterministic screening extrema place this cluster inside a longer, multi-line history of upstream bioburden alert/action signals: an earlier action-level event on SYN-0004 (1.08, Electrolyte Injection, LINE-C, 2024-02) with no deviation record, an invalidated 1.06 repeat with a normal resample on SYN-0014 (2024-04), and seven alert-level results across LINE-A/B/C products between 2024-02 and 2024-12. Common cause is not established by these records alone; the recent cluster is distinguished by same product/line, escalation, open high-severity deviations and shipment of affected batches.

The two prior events each had a preceding alert-level upstream result (PRE-LAB-001 0.79, PRE-LAB-002 0.82) and an alert-level EM result, while the current event reached action level in both the process sample and the environment with an identified gram-negative morphology. This progression is consistent with a persistent or recurring contamination source in the shared manufacturing environment, but the evidence does not identify a source, and no organism observation exists for the two earlier EM rows.

All twelve screening priority candidates are clock-quality flags (missing_source_time) on limit/result cells whose underlying values sit inside their stated limits; they indicate missing elapsed-hours process clocks and limited alignment capability in these lab/historian series, not process faults. Cross-series alignment for the BATCH-099 signals cannot be certified on process clocks; only record-timestamp ordering is available.

No L1/L2/L3 routing policy, severity matrix or release-justification record exists in the scoped package, so any severity or routing proposal from this investigation is advisory and must be reconciled against the site's approved versioned routing policy before use.

BATCH-099's four historian events are all severity 'normal' and inside their expected bands; its PUMP-02 equipment_pressure_ratio (1.0552) sits 0.0448 below the 1.1 limit (11th highest of 100 band events). However, a whole-file scan found exactly 2 of 400 historian events out of range - both PUMP-02 equipment_pressure_ratio 1.24 vs limit 1.1, on SYN-0015 (2024-04-05) and SYN-0090 (2025-01-30, one day after PUMP-02 work order WO-0010). SYN-0090 is the batch of the still-open equipment deviation DEV-0007. Equipment contribution to the microbiological events is unproven but has concrete supporting signals.

BATCH-099 shows no process fault in the scoped historian evidence: all four events are inside their expected bands and labeled severity normal, including the PUMP-02 equipment_pressure_ratio event (1.0552, an upper-tail in-band value 0.0448 below its expected high limit per metric m-b99-margin). A single upper-tail value within band is not evidence of an equipment fault; the two out-of-range events belong to other batches (metrics m-oor-count, m-pr-max).
